summary: All 49 features support a single, coherent product promise: a WordPress plugin that manages per-campaign email opt-in and opt-out consent through trackable action codes. The features share a unified data model (campaigns + per-campaign user metadata), a single admin workflow (campaign management), and a single user workflow (opt-in/opt-out via action URLs). Splitting would create artificial dependencies and destroy the core value proposition.

plugins.one_sentence_promise: This plugin helps WordPress site administrators manage per-campaign email marketing consent by generating trackable opt-in and opt-out links that record user preferences without requiring authentication.
plugins.target_user: WordPress site administrators who send marketing emails to external lists and need to track per-campaign consent while maintaining GDPR/CAN-SPAM compliance.

dependencies.name: WordPress Core
dependencies.reason: Uses WordPress user system, user meta, admin screens, REST API, capabilities, and nonces.

User profile enhancement showing per-campaign consent state (optional)
Administrative visibility of user consent history
frontend_surfaces: Public opt-in landing page (requires action code in URL)
Public opt-out/unsubscribe landing page (requires action code in URL)
REST API endpoints for action code generation (admin-only)
REST API endpoints for campaign CRUD (admin-only)
REST API endpoints for consent state queries (admin-only)
risk_notes: Personal data: Action URLs encode email addresses
Personal data: User metadata contains consent records
Authentication bypass: Public endpoints create users without login
Abuse potential: Public endpoints could be spammed (mitigated by rate limiting)
Privacy: Action URLs must not be logged to third parties or analytics
Security: Action codes must be validated before any state change
Compliance: Must maintain accurate consent records for GDPR/CAN-SPAM
Data integrity: User creation and metadata write should be atomic
plugins.rationale: This is a textbook example of a well-bounded WordPress plugin. All features serve one coherent purpose: managing per-campaign email consent. The data model is unified around campaigns and per-campaign user metadata. The admin workflow is a single campaign management screen. The user workflow is opt-in/opt-out via action URLs. The security model is coherent: admin-only campaign management, public opt-in/opt-out with strict validation. The plugin is independently useful, reusable across sites, appropriately sized, and easy to explain. Splitting would create artificial dependencies (e.g., separating campaign management from action code generation would make both useless). The feature set includes normal plugin components (admin CRUD, public endpoints, metadata storage, security hardening) that belong together.

merge_recommendations.reason: Campaign management features must remain together because they represent CRUD operations on the same core data model (campaign records). Splitting campaign creation from campaign validation or campaign deletion would create useless fragments.

Action code generation and encoding features are tightly coupled implementation details of the same capability: creating trackable URLs. The encoding format, validation, and configuration must remain together to maintain consistency.

Public landing pages and their security constraints represent the same user-facing workflow. Opt-in and opt-out are mirror operations that share validation, security, and behavioral requirements. Splitting would duplicate security logic.

User creation features are shared infrastructure for both opt-in and opt-out workflows. They enforce consistent user creation logic, duplicate prevention, and security constraints. Splitting would create duplicate user creation code.

Metadata storage and state determination features represent the core data model of the plugin. They define how consent is recorded, queried, and preserved. Splitting metadata storage from state determination would make both useless.

Security features are cross-cutting concerns that protect the entire plugin. They represent normal WordPress plugin security hardening, not separate products. Splitting security into a separate plugin would be artificial.

Administrative reporting and visibility features are normal components of a complete WordPress plugin. They query the same metadata that the plugin creates. Splitting reporting into a separate plugin would create an artificial dependency.
